extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians (pro and aspiring), comedy writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing stand-up jokes using the three-part structure (setup, build, punchline), including how to pace, adapt, and use the structure for crowd work and improvisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup
rubrics_metrics.description: This is where the comedian sets the scene and establishes the context for the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The setup should be interesting and engaging, and should grab the audience's attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build
rubrics_metrics.description: The part where the comedian develops the joke and adds details and layers to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The build should be funny and engaging, and should keep the audience interested and invested in the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punchline
rubrics_metrics.description: The final, surprising, and humorous part of the joke where the comedian delivers the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The punchline should be clever and unexpected, and should leave the audience laughing and satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing (gradual build to punchline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the joke so the audience is led gradually from setup through build to the punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By building up to the punchline gradually, comedians can keep the audience interested and create well-paced, engaging jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility and adaptability (mix-and-match parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because setup, build, and punchline are separate parts, they can be recombined to create different jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This modularity is particularly useful for creating varied material and tailoring jokes to different audiences or contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowd work and improvisation readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the three-part structure to adapt quickly when working with the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separating parts makes it easier to improvise on the spot and craft jokes in response to crowd cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and surprise (avoid cheap laughs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A punchline must be both funny and unexpected; cheap or easy jokes undermine quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedians must think quickly to produce punchlines that are clever and surprising rather than relying on cheap laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity and satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-part structure enables creation of more complex, layered jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding details and layers in the build can produce jokes that are more satisfying for the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of the three-part structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Using setup, build, and punchline effectively is an essential comedic skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mastering this structure helps create well-structured, engaging, adaptable, and funny material for stand-up routines.
